items.title: Fixed transcendence degree of the residue field extension is etale local on source and target
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file descent.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: For a fixed integer r, possibly infinite, the lemma asserts that the property of a morphism of germs that the residue field of the point of the source has transcendence degree r over the residue field of the image point is etale local on the source and the target (statement lines 8240-8250). The proof takes a diagram of the shape required by the definition of source-and-target locality and reads off a square of local homomorphisms of local rings, whose vertical arrows are localisations of etale ring maps and therefore unramified, so the two residue field extensions appearing there are finite separable (proof lines 8253-8266). Since a finite separable extension does not change the transcendence degree, the two sides of the asserted equality are equal, which is exactly the required invariance (proof lines 8267-8269). The claim is H2: the argument is short but complete, and it uses the etale hypothesis in a substantive way, through unramifiedness of localisations of etale ring maps and the finiteness and separability of the resulting residue field extensions.
